messages:
sophie: Heads-up — we saw a 95p latency spike on hosted-cluster-us-east-2 around 17:33 UTC for gpt-smallish-v3. Dash shows a sudden kernel selector flip + batcher saturation. Also many requests have no trace attached. Anyone oncall?

ajay: I'm oncall. link to dashboard?

sophie: https://dash.internal/redwood/latency?cluster=us-east-2 :eyes: 95p jumps ~3x starting 17:33, correlates with a rollout window at 17:29-17:31.

deploy-bot: deploy kevin:batching-scheduler v2.3.1 -> production at 17:29 UTC (sha: abc123)

maria: We also toggled `enable_new_kselector=true` in runtime-config at 17:28 during canary. It hit global at ~17:30. Could be kernel mis-selection for short sequences.

kevin: I rolled a change to lower the batching threshold to pack small requests together (aim to reduce per-token cost). Expected win on throughput. Reverting now.

sophie: Profiler snippet (local pprof quick sample):
```
# pprof top summary around spike
kernel_dispatch_ms: 90%ile -> 320ms @17:33
batch_slots_wait_ms: 95%ile -> 120ms
kvcache_evictions/sec: +450%
```

ajay: KV cache evictions up 450%? that smells like noisy-neighbor or same-shard pressure. Do we have eviction logs?

maria: Logs show repeated evict lines: `kv_cache: evict key=shard12-... reason=inactive size_before=4GB size_after=3.6GB`. Also we changed trace sampling earlier to reduce cost — sampling went from 1% -> 0.1% at 17:25 so missing traces expected.

observability-team: Confirmed — we lowered agent sampling to 0.1% at 17:25 to cut cost. Rolling that back to 1% now so future incidents have traces.

kevin: Reverted batching-scheduler rollout at 17:40. Pinning kselector to previous behavior for 24h while we investigate.

sophie: After revert, 95p returned to normal by ~17:46 but throughput for the affected shard is still ~10% below baseline.

ajay: Hypothesis: the lower batching threshold increased instantaneous batch sizes for a mix of short and medium requests, which increased memory pressure -> kvcache evictions -> kernel fallback to a slower execution path for some requests. Any flame graphs?

maria: Quick flame summary: `memory_manager::evict_and_reclaim` ~45% of samples, `kernel_fallback_dispatch` ~30%, remainder in scheduling & I/O.

kevin: Action items (short):
- revert batching (done)
- pin kselector to stable (in progress)
- temporarily increase kvcache capacity for affected shard by +10% (scheduled)
- revert observability sampling back to 1% (done)

devops-bot: incident created INC-2026-0315-512 assigned to eng-runtime

ajay: I'll own the postmortem. Please drop any snippets, flame graphs, full pprof and logs into the incident doc.

observability-team: Note: metrics collector had a GC pause and a ~6 minute backlog of emits during the spike window — adding local disk buffer and increasing collector heap to prevent future backlog.

sophie: Summary: latency spike correlated with batching heuristic rollout + kselector flip. Missing traces were caused by sampling change. KV eviction thrash likely amplified the tail and forced slower kernel paths. Need better canary checks for kvcache eviction rate and kernel-selection stability.

kevin: I'll run a focused load test (mix of short/medium requests) with the new batching heuristics and collect mem/kvcache traces before any further rollout.

maria: I'll audit LRU policy and eviction bursts; add an eviction-rate alarm to the kvcache dashboard.

ajay: Postmortem assigned — target draft in 24h. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
